introduction: On this Sunday, Zechariah speaks of a people who will look on the one they have pierced and mourn for him. In the Gospel, after praying alone, Jesus asks his disciples, Who do you say that I am? Peter answers, The Christ of God. Jesus then speaks of his suffering and calls us to take up our cross and follow him. Paul tells us that we are all one in Christ Jesus. Let us follow Christ, day by day.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our help and our strength. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim Jesus as the Christ of God and follow him on the way of the cross. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are divided by nationality, social status or sex: that they may discover that they are one in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who carry heavy crosses each day: that Christ may give them strength and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who thirst for God: that they may find him and be satisfied. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may deny ourselves, take up our cross daily and follow Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, you call us to take up our cross each day and follow you. Give us the faith to confess you as the Christ, and the courage to walk in your footsteps. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: Take up your cross
reflection.body:
Luke often shows Jesus praying before important moments, and today is one of them. "As he was praying alone," with his disciples nearby, he asks them, "Who do the multitudes say that I am?" Then the personal question: "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answers, "The Christ of God."

Jesus immediately explains what kind of Christ he is: "The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up." And he invites everyone: "If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me."

The cross is not only for great moments of crisis. It is in the small, daily choices to put God and others before ourselves.

Zechariah's prophecy points to the cross. God will pour out "the spirit of grace and of supplication," and "They will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him as one mourns for his only son." John's Gospel later quotes these words at the crucifixion.

Paul shows what the cross and Baptism create: a new people. "For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus."

The psalm expresses the longing that keeps us following: "God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you." This week, notice the small daily crosses in your life, and offer each one to Jesus as a way of following him.
